subject: Request: temporary availability waiver & fixed monthly credit for SpikePilot
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@hypersail.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal <legal@hypersail.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary availability waiver for SpikePilot

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're greenlit to run our SpikePilot (customer-facing load test) in May, but our SREs have flagged a ramp profile that could push sustained concurrency above the capacity we currently estimate. Given the production-like traffic for the first 30 days, we need to request a temporary SLA adjustment so we can operate without repeated breach notices while we stabilize.

Specifically we're asking:
- For May 1 - May 31, adjust the standard availability commitment from 99.95% to 99.50% for the services backing SpikePilot.
- Replace the usual prorated-service-credit % with a fixed monthly credit cap (preferred amount: USD 8,000) in case the adjusted SLO is missed.

Reasons: the pilot will exercise edge cases (bursty KV cache warmup + new batching patterns), and the fixed cap helps our procurement/finance team forecast exposure. We want to avoid frequent re-negotiations or service disruptions during an important go/no-go period.

Attached is the SpikePilot load plan and expected traffic curve for your infra team to review.

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept a temporary concession under these terms (waiver period + fixed credit cap)? If needed, we can narrow the window or agree additional mitigations (dedicated pool, traffic shaping, pre-provisioning).

Appreciate a quick reply — finance needs a yes/no by next Tuesday.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of Product Ops | Hypersail
attachments: SpikePilot-load-plan.pdf
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@hypersail.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability waiver for SpikePilot

Hi Marta — thanks for the context and the load plan. Looping in Laura and Ben to scope feasibility and commercial guardrails. High level: we are open to a time-limited exception for pilots but need to settle the operational mitigations, monitoring telemetry access, and an explicit credit formula so this doesn't set a precedent across accounts.

Quick questions so we can come back with a concrete draft:
1) Is the $8k figure your absolute upper bound for May?
2) Will SpikePilot run from a single region (us-west) or be multi-region?
3) Do you need any privacy/data residency accommodations for the pilot data?

We should have a proposed waiver draft by Monday.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Hypersail SpikePilot — waiver ask (99.50 / fixed cap)

Laura / Ben — hypersail wants a one-month availability waiver (May 1-31) to take SLA baseline down to 99.50% and replace the normal % credit with a fixed monthly credit (they proposed $8k). They want an answer by next Tue.

My suggested approach to keep our risk controlled while enabling the pilot:
- Approve a 30-day pilot waiver, conditional on:
  * Customer runs exclusively in us-west for the pilot (single region).
  * Redwood provisions a dedicated reserved pool (dedicated capacity) for the pilot with a pre-negotiated burst buffer.
  * We provide read-only telemetry (per-route token-level latency and error rates) and an agreed incident contact SLA (15 min ack / 60 min update).
- Commercials: fixed monthly credit cap = USD 8,000. Credit calculation: $X per minute of verified unavailability beyond the 99.50% threshold, up to the cap (we should pick X to align incentives).
- Legal: include an explicit clause that this is a one-off pilot waiver and not a precedent for renewal/enterprise terms.

Operational notes: we can set up a short canary ramp and KV pre-warm window (48h) before the pilot opens. If the customer refuses dedicated capacity, we should deny the waiver.

Attachment: proposed-waiver-draft.docx (contains clause language + credit formula options).

Thoughts? I can push a first-pass to Marta if you OK.

—Avery
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Hypersail SpikePilot — waiver ask (99.50 / fixed cap)

Quick commercial math and risk flags. Agree with conditional approval but recommend tweaking the credit formula:

- Proposal A (simple): USD 1,000 per verified hour of total service unavailability above 99.50% for the month, capped at USD 8,000.
- Proposal B (usage-aligned): 2x the average daily billable token spend during the pilot per incident hour, capped at USD 8,000.

Why: a flat hourly credit (A) is simple and quick for docs, but B ties credits to actual consumption so Hypersail doesn't profit from low-usage scenarios. Both protect Redwood with the cap.

Security/compliance note: we must insist on read-only telemetry and an NDA addendum that prevents any security-sensitive logs from being pulled. Also add maintenance carve-outs (standard windows + 72h advance notice for any emergency maintenance that may impact pilot).

If legal is comfortable, I’d sign off on sending a clean draft to Marta that includes the dedicated pool requirement.

—Ben
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@hypersail.ai>, Ops Team <ops@hypersail.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability waiver for SpikePilot — Redwood proposal

Marta, thanks for the patience — attached is our proposal based on your ask and the internal review. Summary of the proposed one-off pilot waiver:

1) Waiver window: 2027-05-01 00:00 UTC through 2027-05-31 23:59 UTC. During that window Redwood will treat the customer-specific SLO as 99.50% for services supporting SpikePilot only.

2) Operational conditions (must be met before the pilot start):
   - SpikePilot will run from a single region: us-west-2.
   - Redwood will provision a dedicated reserved pool for the pilot (customer pays the standard Dedicated setup fee; we can discount setup fee by 50% for pilot).
   - Pre-provisioning: 48h KV pre-warm / cache priming window and a staged canary ramp (0-50-100% traffic over 24h).
   - Monitoring: read-only telemetry access (latency, error rate, request counts) via a shared dashboard and daily ops digests.
   - Incident communications: 15 minute ack, 60 minute public update cadence during incidents affecting the pilot.

3) Commercials:
   - Fixed monthly credit cap: USD 8,000 (absolute cap for May).
   - Credit calculation: Proposal A — USD 1,000 per verified hour of total service unavailability above the 99.50% threshold for the pilot month (caps at USD 8,000).
   - Credits will be issued as invoice credit applied to the following calendar month.

4) Legal:
   - This is an explicit one-off pilot waiver, non-precedential for renewals or other accounts.
   - Maintenance carve-outs align to our standard policy; emergency maintenance will be reasonably coordinated and communicated.

If you accept these terms we can attach a short waiver addendum and route for signature (DocuSign link included in the attachment). If you need the cap adjusted we can consider up to $10k but would require an additional risk review from finance.

Attached: waiver-agreement-draft.pdf (includes clause language and DocuSign link).

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Thursday (so legal/procurement can finalize DocuSign prior to the pilot).

Thanks,
—Avery
Avery Johnson
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
attachments: waiver-agreement-draft.pdf
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@hypersail.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal <legal@hypersail.ai>, Ops Team <ops@hypersail.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:53:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary availability waiver for SpikePilot — Redwood proposal

Avery — thanks, that reads reasonable. We accept the described operational conditions and the USD 8,000 cap under Proposal A.

Two minor asks before signature:
1) Can the dedicated pool be tagged to the Hypersail account for billing visibility?
2) If verified downtime occurs, we prefer credits to be reflected as a pro-rata invoice reduction rather than a next-month voucher (legal will propose language).

I'll have Legal sign the DocuSign once we get the addendum reflecting the credit application language. Planning team will also send a short calendar with the pre-warm and canary schedule.

Best,
Marta
Head of Product Ops | Hypersail
